Alex / Priya - hey, Dev from the Redwood infra team. Quick answers + a minimal SDK swap snippet below. Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through it.

OpenAI-compatible endpoints:
• Hosted: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/compat/chat/completions
• Model aliases: use model="gpt-4x-redwood" or model="redwood-similar-3b" for smaller tests
• Auth header: Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_API_KEY> (same pattern as OpenAI)

SDK swap (python example, ~3 lines):
• Old (openai): from openai import OpenAI
  client = OpenAI(api_key="<OPENAI_KEY>")
  client.chat.create(model="gpt-4", messages=messages)

• New (redwood-compatible): import requests
  r = requests.post("https://api.redwood.com/v1/compat/chat/completions", json={"model":"gpt-4x-redwood","messages":messages}, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer <REDWOOD_KEY>"})
  r.json()

Notes:
• Most code paths are identical for request/response shapes; only minor name differences for streaming and optional params.
• If you use the official OpenAI SDK and rely on client-side helpers, we also provide a thin shim library (requests-based) to drop in. I can send a small pip package if helpful.
• Rate limits for hosted POC keys: default 60 requests/min with a burst up to 120. We can raise limits for the perf window - let me know target QPS.
• Keys are scoped by project; we support IP allowlisting for hosted keys and bring-your-own-key for Dedicated pilots.

Attached: compat-checklist.pdf (walks through common gotchas: streaming changes, multipart outputs, tokenization differences to expect).

If you want, we can run the perf harness on our infra to remove variability - or you can run the python script we use (I can share). For a fair comparison versus your hyperscaler baseline, please include both single-request latency and tail latency (p95/p99) with identical prompt templates.

- Dev
